t: 3601. Find Drivers with Improved Fuel Efficiency — Editorial
o: We must compare each driver's average fuel efficiency (distance_km / fuel_consumed per trip) between the first half of the year (months 1–6) and the second half (months 7–12), keep only drivers with trips in **both** halves, report both averages plus their difference rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by improvement descending then name ascending. In the example, Alice averages 11.97 vs 14.02 (+2.05) and Bob 11.24 vs 13.33 (+2.10); drivers with trips in only one half (Carol, David, Emma) are excluded. The key implication is that we need per-driver aggregation over two disjoint date partitions, which maps naturally to either two grouped subqueries joined on driver_id or one grouped pass with conditional aggregation.
k: Fuel efficiency is defined per trip; the half-year figure is the average of those per-trip ratios, not total distance / total fuel.
Filtering to drivers present in both halves can be done via an INNER JOIN between the two half aggregates, or by requiring MIN/MAX month conditions with conditional aggregation.
ROUND each output value to 2 decimals and sort by improvement DESC, driver_name ASC.

a.n: Approach 1: Two Aggregated Subqueries Joined on Driver
a.i: Compute one aggregate table for first-half trips (avg of distance/fuel per driver) and another for second-half trips, then INNER JOIN them — the inner join automatically drops drivers missing trips in either half. This mirrors the problem statement most directly and is easy to explain.
s: Build first_half: GROUP BY driver_id over trips with MONTH(trip_date) BETWEEN 1 AND 6, computing ROUND(AVG(distance_km / fuel_consumed), 2).
INNER JOIN first_half and second_half on driver_id so only drivers with trips in both halves survive.
Join drivers for names, compute efficiency_improvement = ROUND(second - first, 2).
ORDER BY efficiency_improvement DESC, driver_name ASC.

c.python:
# LeetCode Database problem — submit as MySQL solution
SELECT d.driver_id,
       d.driver_name,
       f.first_half_avg,
       s.second_half_avg,
       ROUND(s.second_half_avg - f.first_half_avg, 2) AS efficiency_improvement
FROM drivers d
JOIN (
    SELECT driver_id, ROUND(AVG(distance_km / fuel_consumed), 2) AS first_half_avg
    FROM trips
    WHERE MONTH(trip_date) BETWEEN 1 AND 6
    GROUP BY driver_id
) f ON f.driver_id = d.driver_id
JOIN (
    SELECT driver_id, ROUND(AVG(distance_km / fuel_consumed), 2) AS second_half_avg
    FROM trips
    WHERE MONTH(trip_date) BETWEEN 7 AND 12
    GROUP BY driver_id
) s ON s.driver_id = d.driver_id
ORDER BY efficiency_improvement DESC, d.driver_name ASC;

a.t: O(T log T) where T is the number of trips — two grouping passes over trips dominate; joining is linear in group counts.
a.sp: O(D) extra space for the intermediate per-driver aggregates, D = number of distinct qualifying drivers.

a.i: Group all of a driver's trips once and use CASE expressions inside AVG to compute each half's average in the same pass. Require that the driver has at least one trip in each half using HAVING with COUNT(CASE ...). This scans the trips table once instead of twice.
s: GROUP trips BY driver_id joined with drivers.
first_half_avg = ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN MONTH(trip_date) <= 6 THEN distance_km / fuel_consumed END), 2); NULL trips are ignored by AVG.
HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN MONTH(trip_date) <= 6 THEN 1 END) > 0 AND COUNT(CASE WHEN MONTH(trip_date) >= 7 THEN 1 END) > 0 keeps only drivers active in both halves.
Compute the rounded difference and ORDER BY it DESC, then driver_name ASC.

c.python:
# LeetCode Database problem — submit as MySQL solution
SELECT d.driver_id,
       d.driver_name,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN MONTH(t.trip_date) <= 6 THEN t.distance_km / t.fuel_consumed END), 2) AS first_half_avg,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN MONTH(t.trip_date) >= 7 THEN t.distance_km / t.fuel_consumed END), 2) AS second_half_avg,
       ROUND(
           AVG(CASE WHEN MONTH(t.trip_date) >= 7 THEN t.distance_km / t.fuel_consumed END)
         - AVG(CASE WHEN MONTH(t.trip_date) <= 6 THEN t.distance_km / t.fuel_consumed END), 2
       ) AS efficiency_improvement
FROM drivers d
JOIN trips t ON t.driver_id = d.driver_id
GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.driver_name
HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN MONTH(t.trip_date) <= 6 THEN 1 END) > 0
   AND COUNT(CASE WHEN MONTH(t.trip_date) >= 7 THEN 1 END) > 0
ORDER BY efficiency_improvement DESC, d.driver_name ASC;

w: In an interview, lead with Approach 1 because its structure matches the problem narrative and is trivially correct; mention Approach 2 as the single-scan refinement. Pitfalls: averaging per-trip ratios rather than dividing summed distances by summed fuel (the example confirms ratio-of-averages semantics); forgetting the both-halves requirement (INNER JOIN or HAVING handles it — a LEFT JOIN would wrongly include single-half drivers with NULLs); rounding each displayed column independently while computing the improvement from unrounded values vs rounded ones (rounding the difference directly matches expected outputs here); and using YEAR() incorrectly if multiple years could appear — if needed, partition by year too. Follow-ups might ask for quarter-level comparisons, weighted efficiency (total km / total liters), or handling NULL/zero fuel_consumed rows.
